title: A target success rate per question
statement: Give each question a target success rate and treat a result far from it, either way, as a fault in the question.
example: One design targets about 100% success on its first closing question and about 80% on its second.
detail: The closing-questions design sets a success gradient of about 100% for naming the idea, about 80% for finding it in the text and no key for using it: if children fail the first it is built wrong, and if nearly everyone aces the second it is too easy to be worth asking (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-closing-questions-2026-09-24/Closing_Questions_Pattern.txt`). It grounds the gradient in a high success rate in guided practice, which it rates well evidenced and attributes to Rosenshine.
against: No rate has been measured: an audit found the target rates, and whether children actually infer, could not be checked from the lesson files (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/CRITIC.md`).

evidence.quote: Success gradient: about 100%, about 80%, no key. If children are failing Q1, it is built wrong. If nearly everyone aces Q2, it is too easy to be worth asking.
